'''Sealed''' is the generic sealed deck format on [[GEMP]]: decks of 40 cards built from the product a sealed league gives each player. On the Players Committee GEMP most sealed league types are played under it.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-slt" />

* '''Type:''' sealed deck (GEMP sealed league)
* '''Defined by:''' Players Committee GEMP
* '''Card pool:''' the product a sealed league issues, 40-card decks
* '''In use:''' unknown
* '''GEMP:''' ''Sealed'' (<code>sealed</code>) on both the Players Committee GEMP and play.swccg.com

== Card pool ==
The format definition uses the same set list as [[Open]] and a deck size of 40 cards, and marks the format as not a game hall format.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="sets" /><ref name="lib" /> What a player can use is the product the league issues: a league has two series, a player who joins gets the product of every series that has started, and every player gets each later series' product when it starts.<ref name="nsld" /><ref name="slp" />

=== Special rule ===
The GEMP format definitions list this special rule:<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="hall" />
* Once per game, a player may ▼ a unique battleground not already on table.

=== League types that use it ===
In the Players Committee GEMP code, seven of the ten sealed league types play under this format: Premiere-A New Hope Sealed, Hoth-Dagobah-Cloud City Sealed, Endor-Death Star II Sealed, Reflections Sealed, Episode I Sealed, All of the Jedi Sealed and Space Sealed. Jabba's Palace Sealed has its own format, and the two Watto's Cube leagues use [[Cube]].<ref name="pc-slt" />

On play.swccg.com each of those league types has its own format with the same name, and only ''Hoth-Dagobah-Cloud City Sealed'' still uses this one; its product file defines no product list for it.<ref name="slt" /><ref name="slp" /> GEMP's sealed formats are:<ref name="gemp" />
* [[Jabba's Palace Sealed]] (<code>jp_sealed</code>)
* [[Premiere - A New Hope Sealed]] (<code>premiere_anh_sealed</code>)
* [[Endor - Death Star II Sealed]] (<code>endor_dsII_sealed</code>)
* [[Reflections Sealed]] (<code>reflections_sealed</code>)
* [[Episode I Sealed]] (<code>episode_i_sealed</code>)
* [[All Of The Jedi Sealed]] (<code>all_of_the_jedi_sealed</code>)
* [[Novelty - Space Sealed]] (<code>novelty_sealed</code>)

== History ==
The Players Committee's ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' (revised September 2015) gives the paper rules: product stays unopened until players are paired and assigned a side of the Force; in a sealed event each player gives the other side's cards to the opponent, and in a booster draft players pass packs and pick one card at a time. Game time is one minute per card in the deck, so 40 minutes for 40-card decks. The guide lists ten sealed variants, from Premiere Sealed to Secret Squirrel.<ref name="afg" />

The format is in the Players Committee GEMP code and in play.swccg.com with the same definition.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" /> No source gives when GEMP added sealed leagues or who designed the league products, and no league result is recorded.
